chunks: Remember, when We made a covenant with the people of Israel and said: 'Worship no one but God, and be good to your parents and your kin, and to orphans and the needy, and speak of goodness to men; observe your devotional obligations, and give zakat,' you went back (on your word), except only a few, and paid no heed.
ai.seo_question: What were the main obligations in the covenant with the Children of Israel mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal as it encapsulates the core tenets of the covenant (Mithaq) that define the spiritual and social identity of the Children of Israel, linking ritual duties like prayer and zakat with ethical conduct such as kindness to parents and good speech. The mention of 'a small minority' (qalīlan) is often interpreted by scholars as referring to the faithful remnant who preserved the true message, a theme that resonates with the concept of the Ahl al-Bayt as the enduring custodians of divine guidance. This comprehensive list serves as a blueprint for Islamic ethics, emphasizing that true piety requires both vertical devotion to God and horizontal social justice.
